;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Kivu conflict]]
**The [[United Nations]] announce that seven [[MONUSCO]] [[United Nations peacekeeping|peacekeepers]] were killed in clashes with militia yesterday in [[Beni, Democratic Republic of the Congo|Beni]], [[North Kivu]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-congo-security/seven-peacekeepers-killed-in-clashes-near-ebola-hit-part-of-east-congo-idUSKCN1NK2JE (Reuters)]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[Taliban]] kill 30 policemen in an attack on an outpost in [[Farah Province]]. [https://www.foxnews.com/world/afghan-officials-taliban-kill-30-policemen-in-west-province (AP via Fox News)]

;Business and economy
*[[Rail transport in Morocco]]
**The [[Kenitra–Tangier high-speed rail line]], the first in [[Africa]], is inaugurated. [http://www.ksla.com/2018/11/15/morocco-unveil-africa-first-ever-high-speed-train-line/ (AP via KSLA News)]
*[[Criticism of Walmart]]
**[[United States Senate|US Senator]] [[Bernie Sanders]] proposes the Stop [[Walmart]] Act, which would prohibit big employers from repurchasing shares until they adopt a $15-an-hour minimum wage. [https://www.cnn.com/2018/11/15/business/bernie-sanders-walmart-minimum-wage/index.html (CNN)] [https://www.marketwatch.com/story/bernie-sanders-rolls-out-stop-walmart-act-that-would-block-stock-buybacks-until-retailer-raises-pay-2018-11-15 (Market Watch)]

;International relations
*[[Killing of Jamal Khashoggi]], [[Foreign relations of Saudi Arabia]]
**Saudi Arabia accuses five of its officials of killing and dismembering journalist [[Jamal Khashoggi]]. [https://www.timesnownews.com/international/article/jamal-khashoggi-drugged-and-dismembered-in-consulate-admits-saudi-arabia/314621 (''Times Now'')]
**The [[First presidency of Donald Trump|Donald Trump administration]] announces sanctions on 17 [[Saudi Arabia|Saudi]] officials, not including Crown Prince [[Mohammad bin Salman]], for their alleged involvement in killing Khashoggi. [https://abcnews.go.com/Politics/us-sanctions-17-saudis-allegedly-implicated-khashoggi-murder/story?id=59216650 (ABC News)] [https://www.politico.com/story/2018/11/15/trump-administration-sanctions-saudi-khashoggi-992296 (''Politico'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[Cabinet of the United Kingdom]], [[Brexit negotiations]]
**[[Northern Ireland Office|Minister of State for Northern Ireland]] [[Shailesh Vara]], [[Secretary of State for Exiting the European Union]] [[Dominic Raab]], and [[Secretary of State for Work and Pensions]] [[Esther McVey]] resign in protest of [[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|Prime Minister]] [[Theresa May]]'s Brexit plan. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-politics-46219495 (BBC)] [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2018-11-15/brexit-secretary-raab-quits-u-k-cabinet-in-severe-blow-to-may (Bloomberg)] [https://www.telegraph.co.uk/politics/2018/11/15/exclusive-esther-mcvey-resigns-tells-theresa-may-brexit-deal/ (''The Telegraph'')]
**[[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative Party]] [[backbencher]] [[Jacob Rees-Mogg]], with the backing of at least a dozen Tory MPs, says he will submit a letter to the chair of the [[1922 Committee]], [[Graham Brady]], to trigger a [[motion of no confidence]] against Prime Minister [[Theresa May]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2018/nov/15/jacob-rees-mogg-to-send-letter-of-no-confidence-in-may (''The Guardian'')]
